title: fix: point tts-1 aliases at the OpenAI TTS models
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Fix `model=tts-1` / `tts-1-hd` resolving to paid-only `elevenlabs/eleven-v3`; they now resolve to `openai/tts-1` / `openai/tts-1-hd` (Azure, Quest Pollen OK).
- Last 30 days: 1,540 `tts-1` requests from ~95 users, ~14% OK. Almost all failures were the paid-balance 402.
- Azure TTS handled 30 req/min bursts this week without a 429.
- `elevenlabs`, `eleven`, `tts`, `text-to-speech` stay on ElevenLabs v3.

| `model=tts-1` | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Model | ElevenLabs v3 (paid only) | OpenAI TTS (Azure) |
| Price | $100 / 1M chars | $15 / 1M chars |
| Voices | ElevenLabs + mapped OpenAI names | alloy, echo, fable, onyx, nova, shimmer |

Tradeoff: the ~210 successful `tts-1` calls a month from paid users switch to OpenAI TTS; ElevenLabs-only voice names now get a 400.

Part of the audio API cleanup (no new endpoints).

gist.headline: The right voice answers
gist.blurb: The `tts-1` aliases find their intended voices. Quest Pollen works for these calls, and ElevenLabs keeps its own names.
gist.summary: `tts-1` and `tts-1-hd` resolve to Azure-hosted `openai/tts-1` and `openai/tts-1-hd` instead of paid-only ElevenLabs v3; ElevenLabs aliases remain unchanged.
gist.impact: `tts-1` accepts Quest Pollen and costs $15 rather than $100 per million characters, with OpenAI voices alloy, echo, fable, onyx, nova, and shimmer; ElevenLabs-only voice names require an ElevenLabs alias.
